Setting: Conditional Access Changes Not Made By Applications
Recommendation: Review Conditional Access policy changes initiated by an application or service principal rather than a named administrator. Confirm the automation is expected and appropriately scoped, since unattributed changes to security policy are a governance risk. Two common benign explanations before treating this as suspicious: a policy-as-code pipeline, which Microsoft explicitly recommends ('adopt a policy-as-code workflow with source control and continuous integration so changes are reviewable, testable, and reversible'), and the Conditional Access Optimization Agent in Security Copilot, which can create or update a policy from a suggestion in a single click and will appear as a non-human actor. Where changes should be harder to make regardless of who makes them, enable protected actions, which require additional verification before anyone creates, modifies, or deletes a Conditional Access policy.
